name: Tansan
lede: Tansan is a light yellowish brown from the Maerz and Paul color dictionary, and it is among the most common named hues in our painting archive.

sections.title: A dictionary tan
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul record Tansan at #B7916F, first dated 1928, on plate 12 B6 of their 1930 dictionary [1]. The ISCC-NBS system, drawn from that same plate in 1955, calls the block a light brown, within about 5 units of this exact value [1]. The books give no account of where the name comes from, so it stays undocumented here [1].

Its nearest named neighbor in our library is [[camel]], a slightly cooler, less reddish tan [1]. The swatch is a screen approximation of an aged dictionary plate, not a measured pigment [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this tan, as photographed, in 2,561 of 23,781 paintings (10.77 percent), more common than 94 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It peaks in the 1200s, in 22 of 142 paintings, at 1.5 times the expected rate for the 142 paintings we have from that century [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light, in 41 percent of its 1,590 occurrences [2].

[[painter:maarten-van-heemskerck|Maarten van Heemskerck]] is its most devoted painter, carrying it in 5 of 12 of his works here, 4.6 times his home museums' baseline [2]. The earliest matching painting is dated 900, long before Maerz and Paul named Tansan in 1930, which only shows the hue itself is ancient, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. It shares canvases more than chance with [[dusty-peach]] and [[sandalwood]] [2].

origin.source: Maerz and Paul, A Dictionary of Color
